hook.text: You can add '-ness' to almost any adjective—'coolness,' 'weirdness,' even 'purpleness.'

buildup.text: A productive rule applies freely to new words; an unproductive one is limited to existing forms.

discovery.text: English '-able' is highly productive—'downloadable,' 'Instagrammable' appeared without dictionaries.

twist.text: The suffix '-th' (as in 'warmth') was once productive but now barely creates new words.

climax.text: Productivity is a spectrum, not a switch—some rules are semi-productive, working on some words.

punchline.text: Living rules keep making new words; dead rules just echo.

quiz.question: What makes a morphological rule productive?
options: It can freely apply to new words
It applies only to old words
